title: Use COALESCE for Missing Buckets
learning_objective: Learn how COALESCE turns missing joined values into explicit zeros.

tutorial.explanation: When a LEFT JOIN cannot find a match, selected columns from the right table are NULL. COALESCE lets you replace NULL with a default value.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT bucket, COALESCE(count_value, 0) AS count_value FROM buckets LEFT JOIN counts USING (bucket);
tutorial.mental_model: COALESCE reads left to right and returns the first non-NULL value.

guided_example.prompt: Show every bucket and replace missing visit counts with 0.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT b.transaction_count, COALESCE(vc.visits_count, 0) AS visits_count FROM buckets b LEFT JOIN visit_counts vc ON b.transaction_count = vc.transaction_count;
guided_example.explanation: Buckets 1 and 3 have no row in visit_counts, so COALESCE returns 0.

practice.prompt: Return transaction_count and visits_count for every bucket, using 0 when missing.
practice.expected_query: SELECT b.transaction_count, COALESCE(vc.visits_count, 0) AS visits_count FROM buckets b LEFT JOIN visit_counts vc ON b.transaction_count = vc.transaction_count;
